To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) weed control and stemborer control are the most effective means for increasing yields in the Philippines, and (2) the control of sheath blast is not necessary for obtaining high yields, but it may be a good insurance for maintaining high yields.
the rice cropping practices and pest systems of the Philippines are highly variable and that the key pest systems and cropping practices are closely associated with yield.

‘The rice crop system is characterized by two main patterns of cropping practices, which differ by the season of planting and by the use of fertilizer, and by seven main profiles of pests that differ by the presence of sheath blighter, stemborer, and weeds, as well as by the presence of other key pests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the crop system in terms of cropping practices, and the identification of key pests in the context of the cropping system.
the identification of key pests, and of key pest combinations, that are associated with specific production levels and cropping practices.
the characterization of cropping practices and pest profiles and their relationships with rice production in the Philippines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of high fertilizer input, early planting, and weed control is associated with the best production situations.
the cropping practices, and the associated pest profiles, are the result of a complex interaction of the various components of the cropping system.
the analysis has identified key pest combinations that may contribute significantly to yield reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large proportion of yield reduction in the Philippines is due to pests and weeds.
the most effective pest control strategies are not necessarily those that target a single species, but those that consider the entire system of pests and cropping practices.

the analysis of cropping practices and pest profiles is a useful approach to identify key pests and cropping practices, to characterize the cropping system, and to identify the most appropriate control strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of cropping practices and pest management practices is needed to optimize yield and to minimize the risk of yield losses.
it is possible to characterize cropping practices in terms of their effects on pest systems, and to identify key pests that may be associated with production levels.
the analysis of the cropping practices and pest systems can provide a framework for identifying key pests and key pest combinations that are likely to contribute to yield reduction in rice.
